debrief: Debrief: most of my time went on working out the layout in my head (direct insertion between two belts, lanes kept apart, where the poles go). No design in my library fit plates coming in on two separate belts.

Missing: a pole-coverage preview before placing, and a tool to extend a belt line. What failed: connect from the last belt laid a parallel row one tile off instead of extending it, and took belts out of an assembler's output. That cost me a cleanup.

Results: green 15/min measured; red reads 8/min on the dashboard against the 18 I said to expect, and I didn't check it before reporting. Next time I'd extend belts by placing them by hand, tighten the copy box so it skips the source loaders, and measure every block before I quote a number.
I sent the debrief in chat, as you asked, and didn't build anything else:
- **Most time:** working out the green science layout myself, because no saved design fits iron and copper coming in on two separate belts.
- **Missing:** a way to preview which tiles a pole will power before placing it, and a simple way to extend a belt line.
- **Failed:** asking the tool to continue the existing belt laid a separate row one tile off instead. It also took belts out of the green block's belt assembler, and I had to clean it up.
- **Numbers:** green is at 15 a minute, measured. Red shows 8 a minute against the 18 I told you to expect, and I didn't measure it before reporting, so red is only partly verified.
- **Next time:** place belt extensions by hand, copy a tighter area so the saved design leaves out the plate loaders, and measure each block before quoting a rate.

Stopping here as asked. 6 of 8 lanes filled to 21. Copper and gear stalled because I side-loaded them into underground entrances, which doesn't work. Copper is now fed from behind. Gear's end is unbuilt, so the inserters won't restart: it's 5 rows and wood's row-0 run under ground to finish. Should I finish it, or do something else?
Debrief: most of the time went into planning the layout in my head. 8 lanes had to cross on two 2-row bridges, so I ran each bridge row as two interleaved underground chains (yellow + fast).

What failed: 6 of 8 lanes delivered 21 on the first try, but copper and gear stalled. I had side-loaded them into the side of underground entrances, which takes no items. I didn't catch it because I never tested that piece first.
What I was missing: a way to dry-run a layout (simulated pairing and flow) or a grid scratchpad. I tracked about 150 tile placements by hand, so every check was slow.

Next time: feed every underground entrance from directly behind, test any belt trick I'm unsure of on one lane before building the rest, and trace each lane as soon as it's built instead of at the end.

I've stopped building and posted the debrief in chat as you asked. Level 4 isn't finished: 6 of 8 lanes delivered 21 to their output chests (iron, steel, coal, circuits, wood and copper ore). Copper plate and gear wheels didn't.

- **What failed:** I fed both of those lanes into the side of an underground belt entrance, and those take nothing from the side. Each chest stayed at the 1 item it started with until the level reset.

- **Fixes made:** Copper now turns on a normal belt and enters its underground from behind. Gear's ending is half-built, so it doesn't reach a chest yet, and the inserters only start once every input does. I planned the gear fix: run wood's last stretch under ground and bring gear down through row 1. I haven't built it because you said to stop.
- **Debrief points:**
- Most of the time went into planning. Eight lanes had to cross on two land bridges two tiles wide, so each bridge row carries two interleaved underground chains (yellow and fast).
- What I was missing: a way to test a layout or sketch it on a grid. I tracked about 150 placements in my head.
- Next time I'd feed every underground from behind and test any belt trick I'm unsure of on one lane before building the rest. I'd also trace each lane as soon as it's built, not at the end.
I saved the side-loading rule as a lesson for future worlds.
